title: Enhancement: Add native pygnmi MgmtGnmic client and migrate gNMI tests
author: liang-nexthop
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic


Description

Today, gNMI/gNOI integration tests in sonic-mgmt drive the DUT through the  gnmic  CLI binary shelled out from  docker-ptf  (via  py_gnmicli.py  and grpcurl-style wrappers). That approach has two problems:

gnmic  is being removed from  docker-ptf  (tracked in #24328), which will break every test that depends on it.
The CLI-shell path is hard to extend (limited subscribe support, brittle output parsing, no typed error handling) and has had IPv6-mgmt-only gaps (#20395, #20892).
This enhancement adds a native, in-process pygnmi client that talks gRPC directly to the DUT's gNMI server from the sonic-mgmt orchestrator, removing the dependency on the external  gnmic  binary.

Current Behavior

gNMI tests depend on the  gnmic  binary in  docker-ptf  and on  py_gnmicli.py .
Subscribe coverage is limited; POLL/ONCE modes are effectively unavailable.
Output is parsed from CLI text; errors are not typed.
IPv6-mgmt-only setups required test skips.
Proposed Behavior

Introduce  tests/common/pygnmi_client.py  ( PygnmiClient ) plus integration tests in  tests/gnmi/test_pygnmi_client.py :

Unary RPCs —  capabilities() ,  get() ,  set()  return pygnmi's native dict shapes verbatim.
Subscribe — bounded  subscribe()  supporting  STREAM  (with  count / collect_seconds  bounds),  POLL  ( poll_count / poll_interval ), and  ONCE  (drains to  sync_response ). It yields notifications lazily so callers can process or break early; every other pygnmi subscribe option is forwarded verbatim.
Transport/auth — mTLS (CA + client cert/key) or plaintext; per-call gRPC deadlines.
Typed errors —  PygnmiClientConnectionError ,  PygnmiClientTimeoutError ,  PygnmiClientCallError  map low-level grpc/pygnmi exceptions into a stable taxonomy.
Fork-safety — each call opens and closes its own channel, since gRPC C-core threads are not fork-safe and sonic-mgmt helpers (e.g. loganalyzer  parallel_run ) fork between calls.
Enables removing the now-unnecessary  is_mgmt_ipv6_only==True  skips, since the native client handles IPv6 targets.
Value

Unblocks the removal of  gnmic  from  docker-ptf  (#24328).
Gives tests a maintainable, typed gNMI client with full subscribe-mode coverage.
Removes IPv6-mgmt-only skips.
Related issues

Related to #24328 (gnmic removal from docker-ptf)
Related to #20395, #20892 (IPv6-mgmt-only gNMI gaps)
Related to #22396 (broader gNMI test modernization)

Summary:
Replaces the gnmic-CLI-on-PTF wrapper (`PtfGnmic`) with `PygnmiClient`, a native
[pygnmi](https://github.com/akarneliuk/pygnmi)-based gNMI client that runs in-process in the
sonic-mgmt orchestrator and talks gRPC directly to the DUT's gNMI server. This removes the
SSH/CLI round-trip of shelling out to `gnmic` on docker-ptf, drops the dependency on the
`gnmic` binary (which is being removed from docker-ptf to reduce attack surface), and unlocks
`POLL`/`ONCE` subscriptions that the `gnmic` CLI only exposed via an interactive TUI.

Fixes #26015
Related: #24328 (gnmic binary removal from docker-ptf)

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
- The legacy `PtfGnmic` shells out to the `gnmic` CLI inside docker-ptf. That adds SSH/CLI
  overhead, couples the tests to a binary that is being removed for security hardening, and
  cannot drive `POLL`/`ONCE` subscriptions non-interactively.
- `gnmi/test_gnmic.py` was consequently skipped via `conditional_mark`, leaving the gNMI
  client path untested.

#### How did you do it?
- Added `tests/common/pygnmi_client.py` — the `PygnmiClient` client (wraps `pygnmi.gNMIclient`):
  - `capabilities()` / `get()` / `set()` return pygnmi's native dict shapes (thin passthrough;
    no custom result objects).
  - `subscribe()` adds the only things pygnmi leaves to the caller: connection/cert binding and
    bounded collection — `STREAM` (count / `collect_seconds` timeout race), `POLL`
    (poll_count / poll_interval), and `ONCE` (drain to `sync_response`) — yielding notifications
    incrementally. All other pygnmi subscribe options are forwarded verbatim.
  - Normalized-but-string-compatible params via `StrEnum` (`SubscribeMode`, `StreamMode`,
    `GetDataType`, `Encoding`); fully type-hinted public API; context-manager support with
    eager-by-default connect (`connect=True`).
  - Error mapping to a typed exception hierarchy: `PygnmiClientError` base with
    `PygnmiClientConnectionError` / `PygnmiClientTimeoutError` / `PygnmiClientCallError`.
  - Note: STREAM+SAMPLE no longer requires a non-zero `sample_interval` — per gNMI spec
    §3.5.1.5.2, `0` means "lowest interval possible", and pygnmi defaults a missing interval to 0.
  - Each RPC opens and closes its own gNMIclient channel so no gRPC C-core threads survive
    into forking helpers (e.g. loganalyzer's parallel_run).
- Wired `PygnmiClient` into the `gnmi_tls` (mTLS) and `gnmi_plaintext` fixtures
  (`grpc_fixtures.py`) via a new `GnmiFixture.pygnmi_client` attribute, pointing it at the
  orchestrator-local certs in `cert_dir` instead of the PTF-side copies.
- Removed the legacy path: deleted `tests/common/ptf_gnmic.py` and `tests/gnmi/test_gnmic.py`.
- Added `tests/gnmi/test_pygnmi_client.py` — DUT-based integration tests (capabilities; get MTU
  cross-checked against CONFIG_DB, get counters; subscribe in STREAM/count, early-break, POLL,
  ONCE) plus offline unit tests for request-building/validation that need no DUT.
- Added per-test `conditional_mark` skip entries in `tests_mark_conditions.yaml` for the
  DUT-dependent tests (`'bmc' in topo_type`), matching the existing gNMI suite; the offline
  unit tests remain unconditional so they run everywhere.

#### How did you verify/test it?
- `flake8 --max-line-length=120` and `py_compile` clean on all changed files.
- Offline unit tests (no DUT):
  `pytest tests/gnmi/test_pygnmi_client.py -k "build_subscribe or requires_paths"`.
- Ran the DUT-based tests over the `gnmi_tls` fixture: capabilities, get (interface MTU
  cross-checked against CONFIG_DB, counters), and subscribe in STREAM/POLL/ONCE modes.

#### Any platform specific information?
The DUT-dependent tests are skipped on unsupported setups via `tests_mark_conditions.yaml`:
`'bmc' in topo_type` (no front-panel ports / COUNTERS_DB). Otherwise the suite is
`topology('any')` and reads values from the DUT at runtime (no hardcoded platform assumptions).

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?
`any`, subject to the skip conditions above.

### Documentation
<!--
(If it's a new feature, new test case)
Did you update documentation/Wiki relevant to your implementation?
Link to the wiki page?
-->
Updated `docs/testplan/gnmi-uds-transport-design.md` (added the `pygnmi_client.py` entry to the
directory tree and updated `pygnmi_client` references). The new client is also fully documented
in-module with Google-style `Args:`/`Returns:`/`Raises:` docstrings on public and private methods.

comments.author: liang-nexthop
comments.body:
> ### 📊 Overview
> **Files Changed**: 5 (+1067 −28)
> 
> Replaces the `gnmic`-CLI-on-PTF wrapper (`PtfGnmic`) with `PygnmiClient`, a native in-process pygnmi client, wires it into the `gnmi_tls`/`gnmi_plaintext` fixtures, deletes the old `test_gnmic.py`, and adds `test_pygnmi_client.py` plus offline unit tests. Strong direction — dropping the SSH/CLI round-trip and the `gnmic` binary (attack-surface reduction, #24328) and unlocking non-interactive POLL/ONCE is clearly the right move, and the client itself is well-documented and thoughtfully structured (typed enums, bounded subscribe generator, error taxonomy, fork-safe per-call channels).
> 
> ### ✅ Strengths
> * Clean passthrough design: `capabilities()/get()/set()` return pygnmi's native shapes; `subscribe()` only adds what pygnmi leaves to the caller (connection/cert binding + bounded collection). Good restraint.
> * Per-call open/close of the gNMIclient channel to avoid gRPC C-core threads surviving into forking helpers (loganalyzer `parallel_run`) — correct and a subtle trap avoided.
> * Typed error hierarchy with sensible gRPC status → exception mapping.
> 
> ### 📝 Review Findings
> #### ⚠️ Major (should fix before merge)
> 1. **`StrEnum` requires Python 3.10+, repo declares `>=3.7`** (@donghaolicd, `pygnmi_client.py:31`). This is the blocking one, and it's amplified by the **202505/202511/202605 backport labels** on this PR — those branches' orchestrator envs may well run <3.10, in which case this module fails at _import_ time (every gNMI test errors, not skips). Please either drop to `(str, Enum)` mixin enums (3.7-safe, same `str`-compatibility you rely on) or confirm+raise the minimum Python across all targeted branches. Given the backports, mixin-enum is the safer path.
> 2. **Multi-ASIC / supervisor namespace handling in the new tests** (copilot threads on `test_pygnmi_client.py:117,164,189,204,222,242`). `target="COUNTERS_DB"` without a per-ASIC namespace suffix will likely fail on multi-ASIC platforms, and several tests assume `Ethernet0` exists — which it doesn't on supervisor nodes. The `'bmc' in topo_type` skips don't cover multi-ASIC/supervisor. Either add namespace-aware DB access + supervisor/multi-asic skips (matching the rest of the gNMI suite), or scope these tests to single-ASIC topologies explicitly. These are currently unaddressed.
> 3. **`test_pygnmi_get_interface_mtu` reads CONFIG_DB via the standalone `duthost` fixture while the gNMI target DUT is chosen inside `gnmi_tls`** (`:117`). On multi-DUT runs this can cross-compare MTU from a _different_ DUT than the one queried over gNMI → flaky/false failures. Pull the compared value from the same DUT the fixture selected.
> 
> #### 📝 Minor
> * **Stale/unaddressed reviewer suggestions still open**: @ronan-nexthop asked whether the per-testlet skips could collapse to a single module-level `test_pygnmi_client.py` bmc skip (`:3036`), and flagged the warm-reboot skip as possibly unrelated (`:3100`). The copilot bot raised the same **unrelated `test_gnoi_system_reboot_warm` platform skip** (`tests_mark_conditions.yaml:3034`) — that `x86_64-nexthop_` condition is out of scope for a gnmic→pygnmi migration and complicates the 3 backports. Please split it out or justify it in the description.
> * **Docstring drift**: `_ensure_client` says the channel is "reused across calls," but every public RPC closes it in `finally`, so it never outlives one call (`pygnmi_client.py:199`). Fix the docstring to avoid misleading future readers about lifetime/fork-safety.
> * **`transport` comment outdated** (`grpc_fixtures.py:170`): now also set to `"plaintext"`, so the inline note is stale for tests branching on `transport`.
> * **CodeQL "use `with`"** on the `finally`-close in `grpc_fixtures.py:378` — minor; either adopt the context manager (`PygnmiClient` already supports it) or dismiss with justification.
> 
> ### 🧪 Testing
> Good coverage split (DUT integration for capabilities/get/subscribe STREAM/POLL/ONCE + offline request-building/validation that runs everywhere). But per Major #2/#3 the DUT tests aren't safe on multi-ASIC/supervisor/multi-DUT yet, and per Major #1 the whole module may not import on the backport branches — so I'd want CI green on a multi-ASIC and a supervisor-containing testbed (and confirmation of the interpreter version on 202505/202511/202605) before merge.
> 
> ### Recommendations
> 1. Replace `StrEnum` with a 3.7-safe `(str, Enum)` mixin (or raise+verify min Python on all backport targets).
> 2. Add namespace-aware DB access and supervisor/multi-asic skips to the new tests, and fix the cross-DUT MTU comparison.
> 3. Split out or justify the unrelated `test_gnoi_system_reboot_warm` skip.
> 4. Fix the `_ensure_client` and `transport` docstrings/comments; address the open ronan-nexthop/copilot threads.
> 
> ### Status
> 🚨 Changes requested — excellent direction and a genuinely nice client, but the `StrEnum`/Python-version issue (blocking on the labeled backports) plus the unaddressed multi-ASIC/supervisor/cross-DUT test assumptions need to land before this is safe to merge.

Thanks for the thorough review. All items addressed:
1. StrEnum/py3.7 — replaced with (str, Enum) mixin enums; module now imports on all backport targets.
2. Multi-ASIC/supervisor — adopted the coverage fix from #26387: port/DB tests skip on multi-ASIC/T2/BMC until namespace-aware targeting lands (planned follow-up).
3. Cross-DUT MTU comparison — the test now reads CONFIG_DB from the DUT selected by the gnmi_tls fixture.
4. Unrelated warm-reboot skip — removed (cherry-pick churn from our internal branch).
5. Docstring/comment drift and open threads — _ensure_client docstring and transport comment fixed; ronan's and Copilot's threads answered inline.
